name: Saint Christopher-Nevis-Anguilla (1958–1967)
description: A British Blue Ensign — navy with the Union Flag in the canton — charged in the fly with the colony's arms on a white disc: a shield divided per pall showing Columbus's ship, women at a waterfall and a fisherman, with a dolphin crest.
history: The colony of Saint Christopher-Nevis-Anguilla flew a Blue Ensign defaced with the arms granted on 4 June 1957 from December 1958 — the three islands represented in the shield by Columbus's ship for Saint Kitts, women at a waterfall for Nevis and a fisherman for Anguilla. It was replaced on Associated Statehood, 27 February 1967, by the green-yellow-blue palm-tree flag.
